clue.text: Time enchantress showed pluck

parts.note: a witch is a woman who casts spells, an enchantress

explanation.surface: A sorceress, timed in action, displayed courage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pluck' reads as courage after 'showed', but it is the verb meaning to tug sharply.
explanation.definitionFit: To pluck at something is to give it a quick jerk, which is exactly a small sharp tug.

clue.text: German city providing the garb in which I am clad

indicators.note: dressed in, so the clothing word wraps round the other piece

parts.note: wear means clothing, garb, as in evening wear
contracted, I am becomes I'm

explanation.surface: A German city supplies the outfit I am wearing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'clad' signals the garb word wrapped round the contraction of 'I am'; the article and 'in which' are only link words.
explanation.definitionFit: Weimar is a city in Thuringia, Germany, famed for Goethe and the Weimar Republic.

clue.text: Queen is most able to accept

definitions.meaning: the chess queen is the strongest piece at capturing across the board
to take in and understand an idea

explanation.walkthrough: The first reading is chess: the queen is the best piece to capture on the board.
explanation.definitionFit: To take something on board is idiomatically to accept or absorb it.

clue.text: Give it a go — do some entertaining

definitions.meaning: to make an attempt at something
to throw a party; a bash is informal for a party

explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means both to make an attempt and, punningly, to host a party or bash.

clue.text: Policeman taken to corpse -—- he'll nose around

parts.note: busy is British slang for a police officer, especially a detective
a body is a dead person, a corpse

explanation.surface: A detective is brought to a dead body, and naturally pries into things.
explanation.walkthrough: BUSY is old British underworld slang for a detective.
explanation.definitionFit: A meddler who pries into others' affairs is one who noses around in them.

clue.text: Jeer and shout aggressively about drivers

indicators.note: the shouting word goes round the drivers piece

parts.note: to bark is to shout harshly
the RAC, Royal Automobile Club, is a British motoring organisation for drivers

explanation.surface: Fans jeer and yell angrily at the racing drivers.
explanation.walkthrough: The RAC is a British motorists' club.
explanation.definitionFit: To barrack is to shout abuse at a speaker or player, to jeer.

clue.text: Balkan town divided

definitions.meaning: a port on the Dalmatian coast of Croatia

explanation.definitionFit: Split is a Croatian coastal city, and the word also means separated into parts.

clue.text: Bow for short hair

definitions.meaning: a quick curtsy or ... of the head
a short haircut cut level all round

explanation.definitionFit: A bob is both a brief bow or curtsy and a short, evenly cut hairstyle.

clue.text: Take another gamble -have a room-mate

definitions.meaning: to double one's stake on a bet
to share a room or bed with someone

explanation.definitionFit: The phrasal verb means both to stake twice as much and to share accommodation.

clue.text: Credit no longer available to idle

parts.note: tick is informal British for credit, as in buying on tick
something over is finished, no longer to be had

explanation.surface: A shop announces its credit scheme has ended, leaving it inactive.
explanation.walkthrough: 'On tick' is a British idiom for on credit.
explanation.definitionFit: An engine that runs slowly while disengaged is idling, the verb sense of idle.

clue.text: Party left shady nook, getting right away

indicators.note: says the letter for right is taken out of the nook word

parts.note: an arbour is a leafy shaded bower in a garden

explanation.surface: A partygoer leaves a shady garden corner and heads off to the right.
explanation.walkthrough: 'getting right away' removes the R from ARBOUR to leave ABOUR. LABOUR is the British Labour Party.
explanation.definitionFit: Labour is one of Britain's main political parties, so a named party in the political sense.

clue.text: Residence mostly affording accommodation for a deity

definitions.text: Residence mostly affording accommodation for a deity

indicators.note: giving room to something means it is placed inside the other letters
says the residence word loses its last letter

parts.note: pad is slang for a home or residence
a god is a deity

explanation.surface: A home that largely serves as lodging for a divinity.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mostly' drops the residence word's last letter, and 'affording accommodation for' houses the deity inside. Read whole, the clue also describes the answer, an Eastern temple.
explanation.definitionFit: A pagoda is a tiered Eastern temple, a building that houses a deity's shrine.

clue.text: Bringing up the rear in spite of everything

definitions.meaning: coming behind every other one, i.e. last of the lot
nevertheless, despite what has been said

explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means both following everybody else and nonetheless, the two senses given.

clue.text: In a bar, is ale supply given an earthy flavour?

indicators.note: read as supple-ly, flexibly, so the letters bend into a new order

explanation.surface: Does serving beer in a pub make it taste of the soil?
explanation.walkthrough: 'supply' is not provision but the adverb from supple, rearranging INABARISALE.
explanation.definitionFit: Rabelaisian describes bawdy, coarse humour like that of Rabelais, so earthy in flavour.

clue.text: How one might be seen after striking colours

definitions.text: How one might be seen after striking colours

parts.words: How one might be seen after striking colours
parts.note: striking colours sounds like bright hues or surrendering a flag, but here it is being struck and bruised dark and livid

explanation.definitionFit: Someone covered in bruises after a beating is described with these two dark colour words.

clue.text: Ulster vehicle takes a month going up country

parts.note: NI, Northern Ireland, is often called Ulster
a car is a vehicle

indicators.note: in a down clue the month word is read upwards

parts.note: Aug is the abbreviation for August

explanation.surface: An Ulster car carries someone for a month on a trip up country.
explanation.walkthrough: 'going up' reverses AUG to GUA in this down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: Nicaragua is a country in Central America.

clue.text: Kind of collar for immature man

definitions.meaning: a flat collar with rounded ends
a man who will not grow up, after J. M. Barrie's boy

explanation.definitionFit: It names a rounded flat collar style and, figuratively, a man who refuses to grow up.

clue.text: In verse about gnome, only first half is not to be taken literally

indicators.note: the verse word goes round the other piece

parts.note: metrical means written in metre, in verse

indicators.note: only the front half of the word for gnome is used

parts.note: a gnome is a pithy saying, an aphorism

explanation.surface: A rhyme about a garden gnome, half finished, is not meant seriously.
explanation.walkthrough: 'gnome' is not a garden figure but a pithy maxim; 'only first half' keeps its front half, and 'about' puts the verse word round it.
explanation.definitionFit: Figurative language uses metaphor, so it is not meant in the plain literal sense.

clue.text: Cook lazily, without bending

parts.note: to cook figures is to rig or falsify them
idly means lazily

explanation.surface: Someone cooks in an idle way, never stooping.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cook' is not kitchen work but falsifying, as in cooking the books.
explanation.definitionFit: Rigidly means stiffly, in an unbending way.

clue.text: The pictures came in for a hammering

indicators.note: the letters are knocked about into a new order

explanation.surface: The film came in for some harsh criticism.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for a hammering' rearranges CAMEIN. 'The pictures' is British for the movies.
explanation.definitionFit: The pictures is an old British phrase for the movie theatre.

clue.text: Rash on leg had spread

indicators.note: the letters are spread about and rearranged

explanation.surface: A skin eruption on the leg has spread.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rash' looks like a skin complaint but is the adjective meaning reckless; 'spread' rearranges ONLEGHAD.
explanation.definitionFit: Acting headlong means acting impetuously without thought, which is being rash.

clue.text: Round gold coin

parts.note: or is gold in heraldry
a bit is a small coin, as in a threepenny bit

explanation.walkthrough: A threepenny bit was an old British coin.
explanation.definitionFit: An orbit is one circuit around a planet, a round.

clue.text: Endlessly promoting fruit

indicators.note: the word loses its final letter

parts.note: raising means promoting, lifting to a higher rank

explanation.surface: A grocer keeps endlessly pushing fruit.
explanation.definitionFit: A raisin is a dried grape, a kind of fruit.

clue.text: Father about to 'see doctor for assurance

indicators.note: the father word is turned round

parts.note: pa is an informal word for father
lo is an old word meaning look or see
MB, Bachelor of Medicine, is a doctor's qualification

explanation.surface: Dad is about to go and see the doctor for reassurance.
explanation.definitionFit: Aplomb is self-confidence and composure, which is assurance.

clue.text: "1" is a pronoun

definitions.meaning: the impersonal pronoun meaning a person in general

explanation.definitionFit: The numeral 1 is the number one, and one is also an impersonal pronoun.

clue.text: All in shadow tried to move

parts.note: to dog someone is to follow them closely, to shadow them

indicators.note: the letters of tried are moved around

explanation.surface: Everyone in the shade attempted to relocate.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to move' rearranges TRIED to TIRED. 'All in' is British for exhausted.
explanation.definitionFit: All in is an informal phrase for completely exhausted, utterly worn out.

clue.text: Forebears taking part in romances tryst

indicators.note: taking part in says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Ancestors joining in a lovers' romantic meeting.
explanation.definitionFit: Forebears are those one is descended from, collectively one's lineage.

clue.text: Book, but are going in to cancel

indicators.note: says one piece is put inside the other

parts.note: to annul is to cancel or declare void
an are is a metric unit of area, abbreviated A

explanation.surface: A book, but someone wants to go in and cancel it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'are' is not the verb but the unit of area, 100 square metres, A.
explanation.definitionFit: An annual is a book published once a year, such as a children's yearbook.
